title: A Differential Series-Resonance CMOS VCO with Pole-Convergence Technique Achieving 202.1 dBc/Hz FoMTA at 10MHz Offset
problem: Achieving ultra-low phase noise in voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs) for high-speed wireless/wireline communications and high-speed ADC/DACs is challenging; multicore VCOs achieve low phase noise but suffer from area, mismatch, and design complexity, while series-resonance VCOs have not yet been demonstrated in pure CMOS technology.
motivation: Ultra-low phase noise oscillators are essential for next-generation wireless communications, high-speed converters, and frequency synthesis requiring minimal jitter and spectral purity.
method: This design uses a series-resonance topology (connecting an inductor and capacitor in series to peak at one frequency) and a pole-convergence technique (aligning electrical response peaks) in pure CMOS transistor technology. Differential signaling (using paired opposite signals to cancel noise) reduces phase noise (timing jitter) while avoiding the area and complexity of multicore VCOs (multiple oscillator copies).
key_novelty: The pole-convergence technique (which aligns electrical response peaks) makes it possible to build a differential series-resonance VCO in pure CMOS transistor technology, achieving 202.1 dBc/Hz phase noise at 10MHz offset without the area and complexity of multicore approaches.
contributions: First differential series-resonance VCO in pure CMOS technology
Pole-convergence technique for improved phase noise without multicore complexity
Reduced area and mismatch compared to multicore alternatives
